headline: Continued multiple wetland permit reviews, including 11 Cross Street's 168-unit project and National Grid's transmission line refurbishment, pending more information.
summary: The Methuen Conservation Commission continued several Notices of Intent and enforcement matters to future meetings, including the 109 North Street, 397 Transmission Line Asset Condition Refurbishment Project, 11 Cross Street development, and Brook Street Culvert projects, as well as violation cases at 25 Thayer Street, 30 Brown Court, 30 Conte Drive, 824 Riverside Drive, and 91 Lindberg Ave. The Commission also discussed a possible security fence at 120 Lindberg Avenue but took no final action, saying more information is needed.

Continued the Stormwater Permit Application for 11 Cross Street to August 6, 2026.
Continued the Notice of Violation #24-008 / Enforcement Order #25-001 at 25 Thayer Street to August 6, 2026.
Continued the Notice of Violation #25-004 at 30 Brown Court to August 20, 2026.
Continued the Notice of Violation #26-004 at 30 Conte Drive to October 15, 2026.
Continued the Notice of Violation #25-008 at 824 Riverside Drive to October 1, 2026.
Continued the Notice of Violation #26-009 at 91 Lindberg Ave to September 3, 2026.

plain_text:
CITY OF METHUEN 
CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
Minutes of a Meeting – July 16, 2026 
 
The City of Methuen Conservation Commission held a hybrid meeting via in-
person and Zoom video conferencing (VC) on July 16, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. at 
Searles Building, 41 Pleasant Street, 2nd Floor Conference Room, Methuen, MA 
01844.  Present for this meeting were Dave Di Zazzo, Chair; Cara Seaman, Vice 
Chair; Kenneth Sateriale, Secretary; Rachel Lecher, Commissioner; and Patrice 
Friant, Commissioner.  Also present were Chris Parsons, Conservation Officer and 
Michelle Davidson, Conservation Clerk.  Absent was Sandra Bouley, 
Commissioner. 
Chairman Dave Di Zazzo announced that, pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 
2021, this meeting was conducted via remote means in accordance with applicable 
law.  Members of the public body, as well as members of the public, were able to 
access the meeting via virtual means through Zoom video conferencing.  In the 
event that access and participation were not achieved, the Commission would post 
on the City of Methuen website an audio or video recording, transcript, or other 
comprehensive record of proceedings as soon as possible after the meeting. 
 
 
I. Notice of Intent 
 
A.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1323, MCC File #26-004 – 109 North 
Street – Andover Consultants, Inc.  – Nolberto Galicia 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
The applicant submitted a letter requesting a continuance to the August 6, 2026, 
meeting.
Page 2 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the August 6, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
B.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1321, MCC File #26-002 – 397 
Transmission Line Asset Condition Refurbishment Project – BSC Group 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
Andrew Cole, Lead Environmental Scientist for National Grid, and Hannah 
Raddatz, Wetland Scientist with BSC Group (attending via Zoom), appeared 
before the Commission to discuss the peer review comment response letter.  Lucas 
Environmental served as the conservation peer reviewer.  Several outstanding 
issues were identified and discussed in detail. 
Resource Area Delineation: Lucas Environmental identified two Isolated 
Vegetated Wetlands (IVWs), a hydrologic connection with an upland area, and a 
Bordering Vegetated Wetland (BVW) requiring jurisdictional determination under 
Chapter 12.  The applicant proposed completing delineations over the summer and 
submitting revised Environmental Resource (ER) maps prior to construction, 
which is projected to begin in March 2027.  Commissioners agreed these 
delineations must be completed and submitted before an Order of Conditions is 
issued. 
Wetland Flagging: Lucas Environmental noted missing wetland flags in the field.  
The applicant proposed edge-to-edge flagging within 10 feet of access routes and 
100 feet of work areas prior to construction.  The Commission requested edge-to-
edge delineation and flagging of all wetlands as a prerequisite to issuing the Order 
of Conditions. 
Filing Fees and Structure Replacement Exemption: Lucas Environmental raised the 
question of whether the utility structure replacements qualify as "in-kind" 
replacements exempt from substantial enlargement fees under the Wetlands 
Protection Act and local ordinance.  Hannah Raddatz explained that direct embed 
wood pole replacements are comparable in fill footprint to existing steel structures 
(approximately 60 inches or 20 square feet).  Three concrete caissons in wetlands 
represent a larger foundation type, necessitated by soil conditions confirmed via a 
prior soil boring project.  Fill impact percentages were cited as 0.015% increase for 
direct embeds, 0.005% increase in BVW, and 0.003% in BLSF for the caisson 
area.  The Commission requested a formal table documenting, for every structure 
in the wetland, the existing size, proposed size, height above ground, and depth 
below ground.  The applicant agreed to provide this in writing.  The Commission 
indicated this item would not hold up the Order of Conditions once the table is 
provided. 
Turtle Protection Plan and Natural Heritage: Natural Heritage issued a 
determination letter requiring a Turtle Protection Plan (TPP) and adherence to 
National Grid's Operation and Management Plan to avoid a "take." The applicant 
confirmed the TPP is currently under review by Natural Heritage's herpetologist.  
The Commission confirmed its consistent practice of requiring the Natural
Page 3 
Heritage response and an approved TPP before issuing any Order of Conditions.  
The Commission requested a copy of the determination letter. 
Ox Brook / Braided Stream Crossing: The project proposes a construction mat 
crossing of Ox Brook, which features a braided stream channel approximately 15–
16 feet wide at the crossing point.  Lucas Environmental noted the existing plans 
did not clearly show the multiple stream channels.  Hannah Raddatz displayed 
aerial imagery (2023 Google) confirming the braided character of the stream.  The 
applicant described the matting method: timber mats placed on stringers over the 
channel, providing clearance for water flow, anchored by cables in floodplain 
areas, with mats to be removed within one growing season.  The Commission 
requested that the revised plans explicitly show the braided stream channels and 
the proposed matting crossing detail in writing.  The applicant agreed to 
redeliberate and update the plans accordingly.  A second crossing on the eastern 
side of an upland island (across a second river near the Whirlaway Golf site) was 
also discussed.  MassDOT is pursuing a permanent access route; the crossing was 
included as a conservative worst-case scenario. 
The Commission determined that too many outstanding items remain to issue an 
Order of Conditions at this time.  Items required before issuance include: 
1. Edge-to-edge wetland flagging and delineation of all resource areas 
identified by Lucas Environmental. 
2. Completed jurisdictional determination of IVWs under Chapter 12. 
3. Written table of all existing vs.  proposed structure sizes (height, width, 
depth). 
4. Approved Turtle Protection Plan from Natural Heritage and copy of Natural 
Heritage determination letter. 
5. Revised site plans reflecting braided stream channels and construction 
matting details in writing. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the August 20, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
C.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1320, MCC File #26-001 – 11 Cross Street 
– CROSSLD QOZB, LLC – Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc. 
(Continued from July 2, 2026) 
Steven Dresser of Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc., representing CROSSLD QOZB 
LLC; Mark Arnold of Goddard Consulting (Invasive Species Management); Maria 
Johnsenberg of Tighe & Bond (Conservation Peer Reviewer, via Zoom); and Ray 
Comier (Property Representative) appeared before the Commission to discuss the 
proposed 168-unit multi-family dwelling with clubhouse and pool at 11 Cross 
Street.  The site is a former contractor yard described as primarily hard-packed
Page 4 
gravel and heavily degraded.  Plans include stormwater management, wetland 
delineation updates, and an Invasive Species Management Plan for the buffer zone. 
Waiver Request for 35-Foot Buffer Zone: The applicant requested a waiver to 
allow a fire access road loop within the 35–50-foot buffer zone, at the preference 
(not requirement) of the Methuen Fire Department.  The fire department's 
correspondence indicated the loop is a preference for faster egress during 
emergencies but acknowledged the project meets minimum turnaround standards 
without it.  Tighe & Bond (Maria Johnsenberg) clarified that the Methuen Wetland 
Bylaw does provide a mechanism to allow work within the 35–50-foot zone for 
public benefit (health/safety), but the Commission is not required to grant such a 
waiver.  Because the fire department characterized the loop as a preference rather 
than a requirement, Tighe & Bond could not definitively recommend approval on 
that basis.  Chairman Di Zazzo stated personal opposition to granting the waiver, 
emphasizing the Commission's consistent practice of maintaining the 50-foot no-
build, no-disturb buffer and his obligation to treat all applicants equally.  The 
applicant clarified that the project can be built without the waiver using a 
hammerhead turnaround, and that if the waiver is denied, they would not 
implement the invasive species management plan within the buffer zone. 
Invasive Species Management Plan: Mark Arnold of Goddard Consulting 
presented the Invasive Species Management Plan (ISMP), which proposes 
comprehensive removal of invasive species and installation of native plantings 
within the 35-foot buffer, portions of the 50-foot buffer, and areas beyond the 50-
foot buffer where feasible.  Tighe & Bond acknowledged the ISMP represents a 
substantial ecological improvement over existing conditions if managed correctly 
but noted the significant invasive seed bank surrounding the property means 
management must be long-term.  Tighe & Bond recommended a minimum of two 
years of monitoring but strongly suggested conditioning monitoring in perpetuity 
given the persistent seed bank.  The Commission and applicant expressed 
willingness to accept a perpetual monitoring/management condition tied to the 
property title via the Order of Conditions.  Maria Johnsenberg suggested that a 
trigger-based management condition—requiring active treatment whenever 
invasive dominance is observed to be increasing—would be an appropriate long-
term framework. 
Stormwater Management: Steven Dresser outlined the stormwater design: roof 
drains connected to underground infiltration basins sized for up to the 10-year 
storm; a forebay and vegetated swale providing treatment prior to discharge; 
curbing in the buffer zone area to direct runoff to treatment systems rather than 
directly to wetlands.  The site qualifies as a redevelopment site; the applicant stated 
near-full compliance with the 10 DEP Stormwater Management Standards to the 
maximum extent practicable. 
The applicant agreed to prepare a draft outline of perpetual monitoring and 
management conditions and submit it to the Conservation Office, who will forward
Page 5 
it to Tighe & Bond for review and refinement.  Outstanding stormwater plan 
revisions also remain pending. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the August 6, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
Filing deadline for the August 6, 2026, meeting is July 27, 2026.  The applicant 
acknowledged that if materials are not received by this deadline, the matter will be 
continued to the next available meeting. 
 
D.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1324, MCC File #26-005 – Brook Street 
Culvert – TEC, Inc.  – Department of Public Works, City of Methuen 
(Continued from July 2, 2026) 
A continuance was requested pending a peer review response. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the August 6, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
II. CALL TO ORDER 
The official business meeting was called to order at 8:23 p.m. 
 
III. ACCEPTANCE OF AGENDA / AMENDMENTS (IF ANY) 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to accept the agenda.  Seconded by 
Seaman.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
IV.  ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES – July 2, 2026 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to accept the minutes of July 2, 2026.  
Seconded by Seaman.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
V.  NEW BUSINESS 
No new business was presented. 
 
VI. OLD BUSINESS 
A.  Stormwater Permit Application – 11 Cross Street – CROSSLD QOZB, 
LLC – Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc. 
(Continued from July 2, 2026) 
Discussed in conjunction with Notice of Intent Item I-C above. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the August 6, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
B.  Notice of Violation #24-008 / Enforcement Order #25-001 – 25 Thayer 
Street – Moskal and Cavarallo 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
Conservation Officer reported the site is substantially in compliance.  The only 
outstanding item is the property owner's refusal to install conservation markers.  
Scheduling has been difficult due to the owner's limited availability (after 6 PM
Page 6 
weekdays and Saturday afternoons) and the Agent's current workload.  The Agent 
committed to making an on-site visit on personal time within the next one to two 
weeks.  The Commission noted the engineered wetland line plan is now being 
disputed by the owner.  Commissioners expressed a desire to pursue enforcement if 
markers are not installed. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the August 6, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
C.  Notice of Violation #25-004 – 30 Brown Court – Henrique Alves 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
Conservation Officer reported the site is substantially in compliance.  The property 
owner is considering filing an RDA to install a drainage pipe for a storage area that 
currently retains standing water.  As of this meeting, the owner is leaning toward 
simply removing the remaining materials rather than pursuing the drainage 
installation.  The matter was discussed with the owner on the day of the meeting. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the August 20, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
D.  Notice of Violation #26-004 – 30 Conte Drive – Antonio Conceicao 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
Conservation Officer reported visiting the site on July 16, 2026.  A substantial 
amount of bark mulch has been removed from the jurisdictional area.     
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the October 15, 2026, 
meeting.  Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
E.  Notice of Violation #25-008 – 824 Riverside Drive – David Turmel 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
Conservation Officer reported that the property is in compliance and recommended 
to monitor into the growing season.   
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the October 1, 2026, 
meeting.  Second by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous  
 
F.  Notice of Violation #26-009 – 91 Lindberg Ave – 91 Lindberg Ave, LLC 
(Continued from July 2, 2026) 
Conservation Officer reported that he conducted a site inspection earlier in the 
week.  He stated that Dennis Griecci of Andover Consultants is preparing a site 
plan and anticipates it will be completed in approximately four weeks. 
Mr. Parsons reported that the property contains a significant amount of fill, 
estimated to be approximately 50 feet in length and 3 feet in height, located within 
approximately 10 feet of the wetland boundary.  To prevent further delay while the 
compliance plan is being prepared, he made an administrative decision to allow the 
property owner to begin removing the fill material.
Page 7 
Mr. Parsons also noted that the FEMA floodplain mapping was recently updated 
and that the floodplain boundaries have changed since approximately one year ago.  
As a result, portions of the site that may not previously have been within the 
floodplain are now located within the updated floodplain. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to the September 3, 2026, 
meeting.  Second by Friant.  All in Favor.  Vote: Unanimous 
 
VII. CONSERVATION OFFICER'S REPORT 
Conservation Officer reported that he conducted a site visit with a prospective 
purchaser of a 15-acre portion of the property at 120 Lindberg Avenue. The 
prospective buyer is considering constructing an industrial building on 
approximately four acres of the parcel.  Mr. Parsons noted that a substantial portion 
of the property contains wetlands. 
Mr. Parsons further reported that the prospective buyer, who owns multiple 
businesses in Methuen, is also considering agricultural use of the property, 
including raising goats, and has proposed installing a chain-link security fence 
along the 50-foot wetland buffer zone to restrict outside access. 
He asked the Commission whether it would be supportive of a security fence under 
these circumstances.  The Commission discussed the proposal and the potential 
impacts to wildlife movement within the buffer zone.  The commissioners agreed 
that more information is needed before a final decision can be made.   
 
IX. ADJOURN 
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Sateriale and 
seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  The meeting was adjourned. 8:35 
 
 
Respectfully submitted by, 
Dave Di Zazzo, Chairman
